30: using var ctx = new DataContextBuilder().UseSqlite(connectionString).CreateDataContext();

32: using var file = File.Create("orders.csv");

77: ## Formatting rules
78: 
79: * The header names are the **result-set column names** returned by the provider (`id`, `name`, ...), not the CLR property names. A computed column that the query aliases is written under its alias.
80: * A `NULL` becomes an empty field, or [`NullText`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.NullText).
81: * Numbers use [`FormatProvider`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.FormatProvider) (invariant by default), booleans use [`TrueText`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.FalseText), and `DateTime`/`DateTimeOffset` use the round-trip format.
82: * A `byte[]` column is written as Base64.
83: * A field is quoted only when [`AlwaysQuote`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.AlwaysQuote) is set or the value contains the delimiter, the quote character or a line break; an embedded quote is doubled. `\r` and `\n` are always treated as line breaks even though [`NewLine`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.NewLine) may be `\n`.
84: * Output is UTF-8 **without** a byte-order mark; the destination stream is left open.
85: 
86: ## No result object, no boxing
87: 
88: The terminal reads the raw reader columns. The row mapper is not invoked, so a projection whose construction has side effects (a counting constructor, a lazily initialised DTO) is never built. The standard provider column types are read through their typed accessors, so `int`, `long`, `decimal`, `double`, `bool`, `DateTime`, `Guid` and `string` values are never boxed; only a column whose provider type has no typed accessor falls back to the boxed `GetValue`.

90: This also means a projection whose CLR shape cannot be materialised on the buffered path is still a valid CSV shape, because only the SQL projection and the reader matter.
91: 
92: ## Providers
93: 
94: Because the terminal uses the ordinary buffered reader — not sequential access and not a LOB locator — it works on every relational provider that has a `DbDataReader`:
95: 
96: | Provider | `ToCsv` / `ToCsvAsync` |
97: |---|---|
98: | PostgreSQL | supported |
99: | SQL Server | supported |
100: | SQLite | supported |
101: | MySQL / MariaDB | supported |
102: | ClickHouse | supported |
103: | In-memory | `NotSupportedException` |
104: 
105: The [`InMemoryDataContext`](xref:NextORM.Core.InMemoryDataContext) has no `DbDataReader` and can only materialise rows, so the terminal fails closed with `NotSupportedException` — the "no object per row" guarantee cannot be met there. The terminal also rejects a lazy temporary-table source ([`AsTempTable`](xref:NextORM.Core.EntityExtensions.AsTempTable``1(NextORM.Core.EntityBuilder{``0}))), which is executed as a batch rather than a single reader.
106: 
107: ## Plan cache and ownership
108: 
109: Like the LOB terminals, the CSV terminal prepares a **fresh per-call command** and **does not touch the plan cache**: it compiles no row mapper, which is what lets a projection that cannot be materialised (for example an interface entity, `From<ISomeInterface>()`) still export. An ordinary materialising query of the same shape keeps its own cached plan. The reader is owned by the terminal and disposed when it returns; the prepared command is per-call and the context stays open and usable. The destination `Stream`/`TextWriter` is flushed but **not** disposed or closed, so the caller keeps ownership of it (and may wrap it in a `GZipStream`, a response body, and so on).
110: 
111: Cancellation is observed while opening the reader and while reading rows; the token does not close the caller's stream.
112:

using var ctx = new DataContextBuilder().UseSqlite(connectionString).CreateDataContext();

| [`TrueText`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.TrueText) / [`FalseText`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.FalseText) | `"true"` / `"false"` | Text written for boolean columns. |

## Formatting rules

* The header names are the **result-set column names** returned by the provider (`id`, `name`, ...), not the CLR property names. A computed column that the query aliases is written under its alias.
* A `NULL` becomes an empty field, or [`NullText`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.NullText).
* Numbers use [`FormatProvider`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.FormatProvider) (invariant by default), booleans use [`TrueText`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.FalseText), and `DateTime`/`DateTimeOffset` use the round-trip format.
* A `byte[]` column is written as Base64.
* A field is quoted only when [`AlwaysQuote`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.AlwaysQuote) is set or the value contains the delimiter, the quote character or a line break; an embedded quote is doubled. `\r` and `\n` are always treated as line breaks even though [`NewLine`](xref:NextORM.Core.CsvOptions.NewLine) may be `\n`.
* Output is UTF-8 **without** a byte-order mark; the destination stream is left open.

## No result object, no boxing

The terminal reads the raw reader columns. The row mapper is not invoked, so a projection whose construction has side effects (a counting constructor, a lazily initialised DTO) is never built. The standard provider column types are read through their typed accessors, so `int`, `long`, `decimal`, `double`, `bool`, `DateTime`, `Guid` and `string` values are never boxed; only a column whose provider type has no typed accessor falls back to the boxed `GetValue`.

This also means a projection whose CLR shape cannot be materialised on the buffered path is still a valid CSV shape, because only the SQL projection and the reader matter.

## Providers

Because the terminal uses the ordinary buffered reader — not sequential access and not a LOB locator — it works on every relational provider that has a `DbDataReader`:

| Provider | `ToCsv` / `ToCsvAsync` |
|---|---|
| PostgreSQL | supported |
| SQL Server | supported |
| SQLite | supported |
| MySQL / MariaDB | supported |
| ClickHouse | supported |
| In-memory | `NotSupportedException` |

The [`InMemoryDataContext`](xref:NextORM.Core.InMemoryDataContext) has no `DbDataReader` and can only materialise rows, so the terminal fails closed with `NotSupportedException` — the "no object per row" guarantee cannot be met there. The terminal also rejects a lazy temporary-table source ([`AsTempTable`](xref:NextORM.Core.EntityExtensions.AsTempTable``1(NextORM.Core.EntityBuilder{``0}))), which is executed as a batch rather than a single reader.

## Plan cache and ownership

Like the LOB terminals, the CSV terminal prepares a **fresh per-call command** and **does not touch the plan cache**: it compiles no row mapper, which is what lets a projection that cannot be materialised (for example an interface entity, `From<ISomeInterface>()`) still export. An ordinary materialising query of the same shape keeps its own cached plan. The reader is owned by the terminal and disposed when it returns; the prepared command is per-call and the context stays open and usable. The destination `Stream`/`TextWriter` is flushed but **not** disposed or closed, so the caller keeps ownership of it (and may wrap it in a `GZipStream`, a response body, and so on).

Cancellation is observed while opening the reader and while reading rows; the token does not close the caller's stream.

3: /// <summary>
4: /// Thread-local store of compiled query plans (the "plan cache"). Plans are cached per thread and
5: /// shared by every context running on that thread, so the provider (context type) is part of the key:
6: /// the same query produces different SQL and different command implementations for SQLite, PostgreSQL
7: /// and SQL Server.
8: /// </summary>
9: /// <remarks>
10: /// Per-thread on purpose. Together with <see cref="DataContextCache"/> (process-wide metadata) and the
11: /// per-instance expression caches, this is the third cache scope in the context: see the remarks on
12: /// <see cref="DataContextCache"/> for the full picture.
13: /// <para>
14: /// Clearing is process-wide even though the dictionary is <see cref="ThreadStaticAttribute"/>: a
15: /// process-wide generation counter is bumped, and each thread lazily recreates its own dictionary the
16: /// next time it touches the store. A dictionary owned by another thread can therefore only be dropped
17: /// when that thread runs again, which is the strongest invalidation possible for thread-static state.
18: /// </para>
19: /// </remarks>
20: internal static class QueryPlanStore
21: {
22:     private readonly record struct Key(Type ContextType, QueryPlan Plan);
23: 
24:     // The stored key is kept next to the holder so a lookup can hand back the exact plan instance that
25:     // is in the cache. A repeated command memoizes that instance and matches it by reference on the
26:     // next lookup, instead of re-comparing its expression tree against an equivalent plan.
27:     private readonly record struct Entry(Key Key, IDbCommandHolder Holder);
28: 
29:     private static long _generation;
30: 
31:     [ThreadStatic]
32:     private static Dictionary<Key, Entry>? _cache;
33: 
34:     [ThreadStatic]
35:     private static long _cacheGeneration;
36: 
37:     private static Dictionary<Key, Entry> Cache
38:     {
39:         get
40:         {
41:             var generation = Volatile.Read(ref _generation);
42:             if (_cache is null || _cacheGeneration != generation)
43:             {
44:                 _cache = [];
45:                 _cacheGeneration = generation;
46:             }
47: 
48:             return _cache;
49:         }
50:     }
51: 
52:     internal static bool TryGet(Type contextType, QueryPlan plan, out IDbCommandHolder? holder, out QueryPlan? storedPlan)
53:     {
54:         if (Cache.TryGetValue(new Key(contextType, plan), out var entry))
55:         {
56:             holder = entry.Holder;
57:             storedPlan = entry.Key.Plan;
58:             return true;
59:         }
60: 
61:         holder = null;
62:         storedPlan = null;
63:         return false;
64:     }
65: 
66:     internal static void Set(Type contextType, QueryPlan plan, IDbCommandHolder holder)
67:     {
68:         var key = new Key(contextType, plan);
69:         Cache[key] = new Entry(key, holder);
70:     }
71: 
72:     internal static void Clear() => Interlocked.Increment(ref _generation);
73: 
74:     internal static IEnumerable<IDbCommandHolder> Values
75:     {
76:         get
77:         {
78:             foreach (var entry in Cache.Values)
79:                 yield return entry.Holder;
